title: Water cycle
objective: I can name the main stages of the water cycle in order.
explanation: The journey water takes as it moves between the sky, the land and the sea, over and over again.

title: Evaporation
objective: I can explain how the Sun’s heat turns liquid water into vapour.
explanation: When the Sun warms water in oceans, lakes and puddles, some of it turns into an invisible gas and rises into the air.

title: Condensation
objective: I can explain why water vapour turns back into drops when it cools.
explanation: As water vapour rises it cools down and turns back into tiny drops of liquid water.

title: Precipitation
objective: I can describe what makes water fall from clouds.
explanation: When cloud drops grow too heavy, they fall back to the ground.

title: Collection
objective: I can list places where fallen water gathers.
explanation: Water that falls gathers in oceans, rivers, lakes and underground, ready to start the cycle again.

title: Transpiration
objective: I can explain how plants put water back into the air.
explanation: Plants pull water up from their roots and let some of it escape from their leaves as vapour.

title: Freezing
objective: I can explain what happens to water when it freezes.
explanation: When water gets cold enough it turns into solid ice.

title: The Sun
objective: I can explain why the Sun is the engine of the water cycle.
explanation: The Sun gives off heat and light. Its energy is what keeps the water cycle moving.

title: Temperature
objective: I can describe how warming and cooling change water.
explanation: How hot or cold something is. Warm air can hold more water vapour than cold air.

title: Climate
objective: I can explain how climate affects rain and snow in a place.
explanation: The usual weather of a place over many years. It changes how much rain and snow falls.

title: Water vapour
objective: I can describe water vapour and where it comes from.
explanation: Water in the form of a gas. You cannot see it, but it is all around you in the air.

title: Clouds
objective: I can explain what clouds are made of.
explanation: Millions of tiny water drops or ice crystals floating together in the sky.

title: Rain & snow
objective: I can tell the difference between rain and snow.
explanation: The forms precipitation takes. Snow forms when the air is cold enough to freeze the drops.

title: Oceans
objective: I can explain why oceans matter to the water cycle.
explanation: Huge bodies of salt water that cover most of the Earth and hold most of its water.

title: Rivers
objective: I can trace how rivers carry water back to the sea.
explanation: Flowing fresh water that carries rain and melted snow from the land back to the sea.

title: Plants
objective: I can explain how plants take in and give back water.
explanation: Living things that drink water through their roots and return some of it to the air.

title: Glaciers
objective: I can explain how glaciers store and release water.
explanation: Giant, slow rivers of ice that store fresh water for hundreds of years.

title: Groundwater
objective: I can describe how water is stored underground.
explanation: Water that soaks into the soil and is stored between rocks underground.

title: Thermal energy
objective: I can explain that adding heat makes the tiny particles in water move faster.
explanation: Heat is the energy of tiny moving particles. The more thermal energy water has, the faster its particles move.

title: Phase change
objective: I can explain how adding or removing thermal energy changes water between solid, liquid and gas.
explanation: Water changes between ice, liquid and vapour when particles gain or lose enough thermal energy.

title: Gravity
objective: I can explain why gravity pulls water down toward the ground.
explanation: Gravity is the pull between the Earth and everything on it. It makes water fall and flow downhill.

title: Droplet mass
objective: I can explain why a cloud drop falls only once it is heavy enough.
explanation: Tiny drops stay up in the air. When many join together they get heavy enough for gravity to pull them down.

title: Topography
objective: I can explain how the shape of the land decides where water flows and gathers.
explanation: Hills, valleys and slopes steer water downhill until it gathers in low places such as rivers, lakes and the sea.
